# dsh-custom-instructions
English | 中文

Standing instructions for the agent, in every workspace: a **Custom instructions** page inside
DeepS

eek Harness's own Settings panel, whose text is added to the system prompt of every session
in the p

ness's own Settings panel, whose text is added to the system prompt of every session
in the profile.

It is the DSH equivalent of Codex's custom instructions — one place to say "always answer in
Chinese

", "prefer pnpm", "never rewrite a file without telling me first" — except the text lands in
the ass

embled system prompt rather than in a per-project file, so it applies to every workspace,
every new
session, and every subagent, with nothing to configure per project.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then reload the Web GUI and go to **Settings → Custom instructions**.

Installing through the plugin manager (Settings → Plugins, or the market) takes effect without
resta

rting the host; only the browser needs a reload to pick up the new page. Hand-editing a
profile's `d

sh.profile.bundles` instead requires quitting DSH completely first — bundle and patch
layers are com

s` instead requires quitting DSH completely first — bundle and patch
layers are composed at startup.
## Use
| Control | What it does |

| **Enable custom instructions** | Master switch. Off keeps the text but injects nothing. |
| **Intr
oduce the text with a heading** | On by default. A heading (`User custom instructions`) lets the mod

el attribute the block to you; turn it off when the text is itself a complete prompt fragment. |
| *
*Instructions** | The text itself. Empty injects nothing, so deleting everything is a real way to sw
itch the feature off. |
A save takes effect on the next request the agent assembles. Sessions that are already running pick
it up on their next turn.

The page shows the effective state, not just the switch: **Active** when something will be
injected,
**Disabled** when the switch is off, **Inactive** when the box is empty.
## Where the value lives

The three fields are *volatile* configuration fields, so a write goes through DSH's settings
documen

t and persists in the active profile's patch file under the harness home — one document
shared by ev

ery workspace of that profile. Nothing is written into a project directory, and no
project-level fil
e is created or edited.
## How it reaches the model
The plugin registers one `systemPrompt` section:
| Property | Value | Why |

| `name` | `custom-instructions` | One global registration, so nothing shadows it per scope. |
| `or
der` | `100` | Immediately after the deployment persona prefix (`0`) and before every policy and too
l section (`500`+): standing instructions are part of who the agent is, not an afterthought beside t

ool documentation. |
| `interpolate` | `false` | A prompt is prose that may legitimately contain `{{
` and `}}`; the assembler's strict variable grammar would otherwise substitute or reject it. The tex

t is literal. |
| `text` | resolved per assembly | A settings write is visible to the next assembled
prompt without restarting anything. |

The assembler drops empty sections, which is how the off-switch and the empty box remove the text
fr
om requests instead of leaving a stray heading behind.
## Configuration

Editable in the page above; the same fields can be set by hand in the profile patch
(`~/.dsh/profile
s/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Whether anything is injected at all. |
| `wrapHeading` | boolean |

`true` | Whether the text is introduced by a heading. |
| `instructions` | string | `""` | The instr
uctions. Whitespace-only counts as empty. |
## Requirements

- DSH `>=0.1.0-rc.7 <0.3.0-0` (the settings form, the `settings.section` page slot, and the prompt
s

ection registry). The upper bound is deliberate: a later minor release may change rules this
plugin

was written against, and a refused install is easier to understand than a broken one.
- The Web GUI:

the page is a browser-side plugin. The Host half alone still injects the section in
every other com
position, so the text applies even where there is no settings UI to edit it.
## Develop
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`lib/config.js` holds every rule about the injected text and is tested directly; `lib/index.js` is
t

he schema plus one registration; `client/client.js` is a prebuilt browser bundle (plain JavaScript
a
gainst the platform module table, no build step).

Two checks exist because their failures are silent rather than loud: `scripts/release-check.mjs`
rej

ects a bundle patch a YAML parser would drop without a word (a tab, or a `config:` whose keys are
si

blings), and `scripts/verify-bundle-resolves.mjs` proves a listed bundle actually resolves and
impor

ts from the profile — because "the row is in the list" and "the package loads" are different
facts,
and a boot that dies on the second one looks like nothing happened at all.

`test/plugin.test.js` hands the plugin a Cordis-shaped context that throws on any undeclared
propert

y. That is not decoration: reading the live configuration as `ctx.config` throws during
plugin load,

and DSH's boot is all-or-nothing, so the plugin must read its configuration argument
and nothing el

d DSH's boot is all-or-nothing, so the plugin must read its configuration argument
and nothing else.
